title: Nested maps: a gradebook
hints: `AddGrade`: `scores, ok := g[student]; if !ok { scores = map[string]int{}; g[student] = scores }`, then `scores[subject] = score`. The inner map is reference-like, so writing to `scores` writes into `g[student]`.

`Average`: `scores := g[student]` (nil for an unknown student) and `if len(scores) == 0 { return 0, false }`. Sum with `for _, s := range scores`, then `float64(sum) / float64(len(scores))`. `SubjectAverages` needs two maps, `sums` and `counts`, filled by a nested `range`; divide per subject at the end.

`PrintReport`: `for _, name := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(g))`. Inside, collect `parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s=%d", subj, scores[subj]))` over `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(scores))`, then `fmt.Printf("%s: %s (avg %.2f)\n", name, strings.Join(parts, " "), avg)`. Use `Average`'s `ok` to choose the `(no grades)` line.
